courseId.title: Amalgamation & Consolidation of Financial Accounts
courseId.description: Master the accounting for business combinations (amalgamation) and group consolidation (subsidiaries) – essential for CA, CMA, CS, and finance professionals.

sessions.sessionName: Friday: Amalgamation Adjustment Account & Internal Reconst.
Amalgamation of A Ltd & B Ltd: Purchase vs Merger comparison
Friday: Consolidation with Step Acquisition & Disposal
Final Project: Group Consolidation (Parent + 2 Subs): Full consolidated accounts

days.learning: 🎯 1h: Meaning, reasons for amalgamation. Types: amalgamation in nature of merger (pooling of interests) vs purchase (acquisition). Legal framework (Companies Act).
🎯 1h: Conditions for merger method. Accounting: assets, liabilities recorded at book values. Calculation of purchase consideration. Journal entries in transferee books.
🎯 1h: When purchase method applies. Fair value adjustments. Goodwill or capital reserve calculation. Entry for discharge of consideration (shares, cash, etc.).
🎯 1h: Net assets method vs net payment method. Treatment of inter‑company holdings. Illustration: calculate consideration and pass journal entries.
🎯 1h: Amalgamation adjustment account (to preserve reserves). Difference between amalgamation and internal reconstruction (capital reduction).
🎯 1h: Solve a full amalgamation problem (merger method): two companies combine, prepare ledger accounts and balance sheet of new company.

days.dayName: Amalgamation of A Ltd & B Ltd
days.learning: ✅ Given balance sheets of two companies, do the following: ➤ Compute purchase consideration under both net assets method and net payment method. ➤ Prepare journal entries and the new company’s balance sheet using purchase method. ➤ Re‑do using pooling of interests method (if conditions met). ➤ Write a short note on which method is preferable and why. ➤ Deliver: Excel working + journal entries + final balance sheets.
days.projectBadge: 📝 Assessment: 15 MCQs (types of amalgamation, goodwill, consideration methods, accounting entries).

curriculum.weekTitle: ⚡ Week 2 – Consolidation of Financial Statements (Group Accounts)

days.learning: 🎯 1h: Control concept. Subsidiary vs associate. Consolidated balance sheet: eliminate investment against equity, calculate goodwill/NC interest (NCI).
🎯 1h: Proportionate share of subsidiary’s net assets. Two methods: partial goodwill vs full goodwill (IFRS). Calculate NCI at acquisition and post‑acquisition.
🎯 1h: Unrealised profit on inventory, inter‑company receivables/payables, inter‑company dividends. Elimination entries.
🎯 1h: Add parent and subsidiary P&L line by line. Remove inter‑company sales and dividends. Apportion NCI share of profit.
🎯 1h: Piecemeal acquisition, change in ownership without loss of control. Partial disposal – gain/loss calculation in P&L.
🎯 1h: Standard consolidation working table (CW) – goodwill, NCI, retained earnings. Solve a simple group with one subsidiary.

✅ Prepare consolidated balance sheet and income statement for P Ltd with S1 Ltd (80%) and S2 Ltd (60%): ➤ Calculate goodwill and NCI for both subsidiaries. ➤ Eliminate inter‑company sales (S1 sold to P – 40% unsold). ➤ Eliminate inter‑company receivables/payables. ➤ Compute consolidated retained earnings and NCI share. ➤ Deliver: Working papers (goodwill, NCI, elimination journal entries) + final consolidated statements in Excel/Word.
days.projectBadge: 📝 Final Assessment: 20 questions (consolidation workings, NCI, unrealised profit, step acquisition) + one case‑study analysis.

courseId.title: Entrepreneurship for Product‑Based Company
courseId.description: From idea to launch: customer discovery, MVP, product‑market fit, business models, fundraising, and growth – essential for aspiring founders and product managers.

sessions.sessionName: Product Idea Validation: Problem interview + MVP sketch
Final Project: Product Business Plan: From idea to pitch deck

days.learning: 🎯 1h: Entrepreneurial mindset. Identify pain points, market gaps. Problem vs solution. Case studies of product startups (Dropbox, Slack).
🎯 1h: Lean Startup: get out of the building. How to conduct customer interviews. Build a problem hypothesis. Example interview script.
🎯 1h: Value Proposition Canvas. Create user personas. Jobs‑to‑be‑done framework. Differentiate from competitors.
🎯 1h: What is MVP? Types: concierge, Wizard of Oz, landing page, video. Prioritise features. Example: Zappos, Buffer.
🎯 1h: Definition of product‑market fit (PMF). Indicators: retention, NPS, “must‑have” survey. Sean Ellis test.
🎯 1h: Subscription, freemium, transaction fee, licensing, advertising. Pricing strategies (value‑based, cost‑plus).

✅ Validate a product idea of your choice: ➤ Write down a problem you want to solve (target market). ➤ Create a customer interview guide and interview 3 potential users. ➤ Summarise findings – is the problem real? ➤ Sketch an MVP (wireframe or landing page mockup) to test the solution. ➤ Deliver: 1‑page validation report + MVP sketch (paper or digital).
days.projectBadge: 📝 Assessment: 15 MCQs (lean startup, MVP types, value prop, PMF indicators, business models).

days.learning: 🎯 1h: Channels: inbound, outbound, partnerships. Launch sequence (beta, soft launch, full launch). Case: how Dropbox grew via referral.
🎯 1h: Unit economics (CAC, LTV, gross margin). Burn rate, runway. Simple P&L for a product startup.
🎯 1h: Stages: pre‑seed, seed, Series A/B. Angel investors vs VCs. Pitch deck essentials. Term sheet basics (valuation, dilution).
🎯 1h: Co‑founder equity split. Hiring first employees. Remote vs in‑office. Startup culture and values.
🎯 1h: AARRR metrics (acquisition, activation, retention, referral, revenue). Cohort analysis. Pirate metrics.
🎯 1h: When to pivot vs persevere. Types of pivots (zoom‑in, customer segment, platform). Learning from failure (case: Webvan vs Amazon).

✅ Create a mini business plan for a product‑based startup: ➤ Problem & solution (from Week 1 project). ➤ Target market & personas. ➤ MVP description & product roadmap. ➤ Business model & pricing. ➤ Go‑to‑market plan (first 90 days). ➤ Financial projections (simple spreadsheet: revenue, costs, runway). ➤ Optional: create a 5‑slide pitch deck. ➤ Deliver: PDF document (2‑3 pages) + optional pitch deck.
days.projectBadge: 📝 Final Assessment: 20 questions (GTM, unit economics, fundraising stages, metrics, pivots) + case analysis of a real product startup.

courseName: Inventory Control & Management for Supply Chain

courseId.title: Inventory Control & Management for Supply Chain
courseId.description: Master inventory fundamentals, EOQ, safety stock, ABC analysis, and modern supply chain techniques – essential for operations, logistics, and SCM roles.

sessions.sessionName: Friday: Periodic vs Perpetual Review Systems
EOQ & ABC Implementation: Excel / Python case study
Wednesday: Bullwhip Effect & Supply Chain Coordination
Final Project: Inventory Policy Design: Stochastic demand + service level

days.learning: 🎯 1h: What is inventory? Types: raw material, WIP, finished goods. Holding cost, ordering cost, shortage cost. Inventory turnover ratio.
🎯 1h: EOQ formula derivation and assumptions. Calculate optimal order quantity, total cost, reorder point (constant demand). Solve 2 problems.
🎯 1h: Deterministic ROP. Lead time demand. Basic safety stock formula (service level approach). Use normal distribution table.
🎯 1h: Classify inventory into A (high value), B, C items based on annual consumption value. Policy differences for each class.
🎯 1h: P‑system (fixed interval) vs Q‑system (fixed quantity). Advantages and trade‑offs. When to use each.
🎯 1h: All‑units quantity discounts. Calculate optimal order quantity when price breaks exist. Step‑by‑step procedure.

✅ Given historical demand, costs, and item list for a warehouse: ➤ Calculate EOQ and total annual inventory cost for top 5 SKUs. ➤ Perform ABC analysis on 20 items (compute annual usage value, sort, classify). ➤ Recommend reorder policy (Q‑system or P‑system) for each class. ➤ Deliver: Excel workbook or Python notebook with calculations + one‑page summary.
days.projectBadge: 📝 Assessment: 15 MCQs (inventory costs, EOQ, ROP, ABC, quantity discounts).

curriculum.weekTitle: ⚡ Week 2 – Uncertainty, Service Levels & Modern Techniques

days.learning: 🎯 1h: Cycle service level (CSL) vs fill rate. Calculate safety stock for desired CSL. Newsvendor model intuition.
🎯 1h: Moving average, exponential smoothing. Forecast error (MAD, MSE). Use forecast to set ROP.
🎯 1h: Causes of bullwhip effect (demand signal processing, order batching). Countermeasures: VMI, information sharing.
🎯 1h: VMI concept, benefits, risks. Just‑in‑Time inventory – lean philosophy, Kanban, reduced waste.
🎯 1h: Centralised vs decentralised. Safety stock pooling effect. Echelon vs installation stock.
🎯 1h: Key metrics: inventory turns, days of inventory, obsolete %, service level. Introduction to ERP (SAP MM) and WMS.

✅ Design an inventory control policy for a retailer with uncertain demand: ➤ Given daily demand (normal distribution) and lead time of 5 days. ➤ Calculate safety stock for 95% service level. ➤ Determine reorder point and order quantity (EOQ with uncertainty). ➤ Simulate 50 days of inventory (use Excel or Python) and report stockout frequency. ➤ Deliver: simulation spreadsheet/script + a policy recommendation memo.
days.projectBadge: 📝 Final Assessment: 20 questions (service level, safety stock, bullwhip, VMI, JIT, multi‑echelon) + case analysis on a real supply chain.

courseId.title: ️ Kubernetes in 2 Weeks
courseId.description: Hands‑on, job‑ready track — no prior K8s experience needed, but basic Docker & Linux helps.

sessions.sessionName: Final Project & Certification Readiness: Project + Quiz

days.learning: 🎯 1h: What is Kubernetes? Control Plane vs Worker Nodes. Install Minikube & kubectl. Run kubectl get nodes.
🎯 1h: Pod as smallest unit. Write first pod.yaml, apply, inspect (kubectl get pods -o wide). Port‑forward to see app.
🎯 1h: Create Deployment with 2 replicas. Scale to 3. Perform rolling update (change image). Rollback.
🎯 1h: ClusterIP, NodePort, LoadBalancer. Expose deployment via NodePort and curl from outside.
🎯 1h: Create namespace, switch context. Use labels to filter pods (-l app=myapp). Resource quotas intro.
🎯 1h: Deploy nginx + custom web app. Expose via NodePort. Simulate a rolling update. Verify replicas.

✅ Project 1 – Zero‑downtime web app ➤ Deploy a simple “Hello K8s” app (any image) with 3 replicas. ➤ Expose via NodePort service. ➤ Perform two rolling updates (change text/version) without downtime. ➤ Submit: YAML files + screenshot of rollout history.
days.projectBadge: 📝 Assessment: Short quiz (10 questions on pods, deployments, services).

days.learning: 🎯 1h: Store config as ConfigMap, inject into pod as env. Create Secret (base64), mount as volume.
🎯 1h: Create PersistentVolume and PersistentVolumeClaim. Deploy MySQL with PVC – data survives pod deletion.
🎯 1h: livenessProbe & readinessProbe. Set CPU/memory requests/limits. Observe pod behaviour under stress.
🎯 1h: Install NGINX Ingress (Minikube addon). Route traffic to two services using path‑based rules.
🎯 1h: Install Helm, add repo (bitnami). Deploy a chart (e.g. WordPress), customize with values.yaml.
🎯 1h: Create ServiceAccount, Role, RoleBinding. Practice debug: kubectl describe, logs, events.

✅ Final Project – Multi‑tier app on Kubernetes ➤ Deploy a frontend (React/Nginx) + backend (Node.js/Python) + MongoDB with persistent storage. ➤ Use ConfigMap for backend config, Secret for DB password. ➤ Expose frontend via Ingress. ➤ Implement liveness/readiness probes for backend. ➤ Deliver: All YAML manifests + a short deployment guide.
days.projectBadge: 📝 Final Assessment: 20 multiple‑choice questions + 2 troubleshooting scenarios (kubectl debug).

courseId.title: Statistics for AI & Machine Learning
courseId.description: Master the statistical foundations required for data science, ML model interpretation, and AI research – essential for aspiring data scientists and ML engineers.

sessions.sessionName: Monday: Measures of Central Tendency & Dispersion
Exploratory Data Analysis: Descriptive stats + visualisation
Saturday: Bayesian Statistics Intro for ML
Final Project: A/B Testing & Regression Analysis: Real‑world statistical decision

days.learning: 🎯 1h: Mean, median, mode. Variance, standard deviation, range, IQR. Use Python (NumPy/pandas) to compute on a dataset.
🎯 1h: Histograms, box plots, scatter plots, bar charts. Use matplotlib/seaborn. Identify skewness, outliers.
🎯 1h: Sample space, events, conditional probability, Bayes' theorem. Mutually exclusive vs independent events.
🎯 1h: Discrete vs continuous random variables. Probability mass function, probability density function. Expected value and variance.
🎯 1h: Binomial, Poisson, Normal (Gaussian), Exponential. Properties and real‑world use cases (e.g., Normal in ML).
🎯 1h: Statement and intuition. Why CLT enables confidence intervals and hypothesis testing. Simulate in Python.

✅ Take a real dataset (e.g., Iris, housing, or any Kaggle dataset): ➤ Compute mean, median, mode, variance, standard deviation for each numeric column. ➤ Identify outliers using IQR. ➤ Create histograms, box plots, and a scatter plot matrix. ➤ Write a short summary of distributions and skewness. ➤ Deliver: Jupyter Notebook with code and markdown explanations.
days.projectBadge: 📝 Assessment: 15 MCQs (central tendency, variance, probability rules, CLT, distribution properties).

curriculum.weekTitle: ⚡ Week 2 – Inferential Stats, Hypothesis Testing, Regression

days.learning: 🎯 1h: Population vs sample. Sampling distribution. Construct and interpret 95% confidence interval for mean/proportion.
🎯 1h: Null vs alternative hypothesis, p‑value, significance level (α). Type I and Type II errors. One‑tailed vs two‑tailed tests.
🎯 1h: One‑sample t‑test, two‑sample t‑test, paired t‑test. ANOVA for comparing multiple groups. Use Python (scipy.stats).
🎯 1h: Pearson correlation coefficient, Spearman rank correlation. Covariance matrix. Interpret correlation in feature selection for ML.
🎯 1h: Simple linear regression: slope, intercept, R², residuals. Assumptions. Connection to correlation.
🎯 1h: Prior, likelihood, posterior. Naïve Bayes classifier intuition. Comparison with frequentist approach.

days.dayName: Final Project: A/B Testing & Regression Analysis
days.learning: ✅ Choose a business problem (e.g., website conversion A/B test or house price prediction): ➤ Perform hypothesis testing (t‑test) on two groups – report p‑value and conclusion. ➤ Build a simple linear regression model using sklearn/statsmodels. ➤ Interpret coefficients, R², and p‑values for features. ➤ Write a one‑page report: “Did the treatment have a statistically significant effect?” ➤ Deliver: Python script/notebook + PDF report.
days.projectBadge: 📝 Final Assessment: 20 questions (CI, hypothesis testing, p‑value, t‑test, correlation, regression, Bayesian basics) + case study interpretation.

courseName: ️ Web Scraping & Data Pipelines in 2 Weeks

courseId.title: ️ Web Scraping & Data Pipelines in 2 Weeks
courseId.description: Learn to extract data from websites, build ETL pipelines, schedule jobs, and store data – essential for data engineering, analytics, and automation roles.

sessions.sessionName: Scrape Bookstore / Job Listings: Full scraping pipeline
Thursday: Scheduling Pipelines (Cron / Apache Airflow basics)
Final Project: Automated News/Weather Pipeline: Scraping + ETL + Scheduling

days.learning: 🎯 1h: How web servers work. GET/POST requests. Use `requests` library to fetch a webpage. Inspect HTML structure (Chrome DevTools).
🎯 1h: Parse HTML with BeautifulSoup. Find elements by tag, class, id. Extract text, attributes. Navigate the parse tree.
🎯 1h: Scrape data from Wikipedia tables. Use `find_all('table')`, convert to pandas DataFrame. Save as CSV.
🎯 1h: Loop through multiple pages (changing URL parameters). Identify AJAX calls (Network tab). Use `requests` with query strings.
🎯 1h: Install Scrapy, create a project, define a spider. Extract items and export as JSON/CSV. Scrapy shell for testing.
🎯 1h: Ethics and legality of scraping. Set custom headers, delay between requests. Use `time.sleep` or Scrapy `DOWNLOAD_DELAY`.

✅ Build a scraper for a public website (e.g., books.toscrape.com or a job board): ➤ Scrape all book titles, prices, ratings from at least 5 pages. ➤ Handle pagination automatically. ➤ Save output to CSV and JSON. ➤ Add a 1‑second delay between requests. ➤ Deliver: Python script + CSV/JSON files + a short readme.
days.projectBadge: 📝 Assessment: 15 MCQs (HTTP methods, BeautifulSoup selectors, Scrapy vs requests, scraping ethics).

days.learning: 🎯 1h: Extract, Transform, Load. Use pandas to clean scraped data: handle missing values, change data types, remove duplicates.
🎯 1h: Create tables, insert scraped data into SQLite (or PostgreSQL). Use `sqlalchemy` and `pandas.to_sql`.
🎯 1h: Avoid duplicates when scraping daily. Use `ON CONFLICT` or check existing records before insert.
🎯 1h: Schedule a Python script with cron (Linux/macOS) or Task Scheduler (Windows). Introduction to Airflow DAGs (one simple DAG).
🎯 1h: Try‑except for network failures. Retry logic. Python logging module to record pipeline runs and errors.
🎯 1h: Scrape → clean → store in DB → schedule daily. End‑to‑end script with functions for each stage.

✅ Build a complete automated data pipeline: ➤ Scrape a news site or weather forecast every hour (or daily). ➤ Clean and transform the data (extract headlines, temperature, etc.). ➤ Store in a SQLite database with timestamps. ➤ Implement incremental loading (no duplicates). ➤ Schedule the script to run automatically (cron or Task Scheduler). ➤ Deliver: Python script, database schema, scheduler configuration, and a log file showing 3 successful runs.
days.projectBadge: 📝 Final Assessment: 20 questions (ETL steps, incremental loading, scheduling tools, error handling) + design a pipeline for a given scenario.

courseId.title: PHP for Backend Development
courseId.description: Learn PHP from basics to building dynamic web applications, databases, sessions, and REST APIs – essential for backend developer roles.

sessions.sessionName: Final Project: Task Manager / Blog System: Full CRUD + Auth + API

days.learning: 🎯 1h: Install XAMPP/WAMP or use online PHP sandbox. Variables, data types, echo/print, comments. Embed PHP in HTML.
🎯 1h: Arithmetic, comparison, logical operators. if/else, switch. for, while, foreach loops. Build a simple number guessing script.
🎯 1h: Indexed, associative, multidimensional arrays. Array functions: count, push, sort, merge. String functions: strlen, strpos, explode, implode.
🎯 1h: Define and call functions, parameters, return values. Global vs local scope. Built‑in date, math functions.
🎯 1h: Create HTML form, handle submission with PHP. Access $_GET and $_POST. Sanitize user input (htmlspecialchars, filter_var).
🎯 1h: Set/read cookies. Start a session, store user data, destroy session. Build a simple login/logout counter.

✅ Build a small web app: ➤ A feedback form (name, rating, comment). ➤ Store submitted feedback in a session array (no database yet). ➤ Display all feedback on a separate dashboard page. ➤ Include a “reset session” button. ➤ Deliver: PHP files (index.php, dashboard.php, style.css optional).
days.projectBadge: 📝 Assessment: 15 MCQs (PHP syntax, superglobals, sessions, arrays, forms).

curriculum.weekTitle: ⚡ Week 2 – MySQL Integration, Security, REST APIs

days.learning: 🎯 1h: Create database, tables (users, products). CRUD SQL queries (INSERT, SELECT, UPDATE, DELETE).
🎯 1h: Connect to MySQL using PDO. Write prepared statements to prevent SQL injection. Fetch data as associative array.
🎯 1h: Create a “products” table. Build list page (read) and add product form (create). Display products from DB.
🎯 1h: Edit product: pre‑populate form, update query. Delete product with confirmation. Flash messages for success/error.
🎯 1h: User registration: hash password with password_hash(). Login: verify with password_verify(). Protect pages with session check.
🎯 1h: Create a simple API endpoint that returns JSON. Read GET parameters, handle POST to insert. Test with Postman.

days.dayName: Final Project: Task Manager / Blog System
days.learning: ✅ Build a complete backend system (choose one): ➤ Task manager: users can register/login, create/edit/delete tasks, mark complete. ➤ Or simple blog: posts with title, content, author, timestamp. ➤ Must include: authentication, database (MySQL), CRUD for posts/tasks. ➤ Optional: create a REST endpoint to fetch posts/tasks as JSON. ➤ Deliver: All PHP source files, database SQL dump, and a README with setup steps.
days.projectBadge: 📝 Final Assessment: 20 questions (PDO, SQL injection, sessions, password hashing, REST APIs, file structure).

courseId.title: JavaScript for iOS/Android (React Native)
courseId.description: Build cross‑platform mobile apps for iOS and Android using JavaScript and React Native – essential for frontend and mobile development roles.

sessions.sessionName: Friday: React Native Setup & Core Components
Saturday: Styling & Flexbox in React Native
Personal Portfolio App: Basic UI + Data Fetching
Wednesday: Device Features: Camera & Image Picker
Final Project: Note‑Taking or Task Manager App: Full CRUD with Navigation & Storage

days.learning: 🎯 1h: Variables (let, const), arrow functions, template literals, destructuring, spread/rest operators. Practice writing small ES6+ snippets in a REPL or browser console. (Modern JS is the foundation of React Native.)
🎯 1h: Fetch data from a public API using fetch(). Understand Promises, then/catch, and async/await. Mobile apps heavily rely on async operations for network calls and device APIs.
🎯 1h: Functional components, JSX syntax, props, and basic state with useState. Build a simple interactive counter component.
🎯 1h: useEffect for side effects (data fetching, subscriptions). Understand the dependency array. Also introduce useRef and useCallback briefly.
🎯 1h: Install Node.js, watchman, and set up Expo Go on your phone. Create a new Expo project. Explore core components: View, Text, Image, ScrollView, FlatList.
🎯 1h: Use StyleSheet.create, inline styles, Flexbox layout (justifyContent, alignItems, flexDirection). Build a simple profile card UI with image, text, and button.

✅ Build a simple mobile portfolio app: ➤ Create a new Expo project. ➤ Design a profile screen with avatar, name, bio, and social links using Flexbox. ➤ Fetch a list of your GitHub repositories (or any public data) using fetch() and display them in a FlatList. ➤ Add a loading indicator while data loads. ➤ Deliver: Expo project folder (or GitHub repo) + a short screen recording of the app running on a simulator or physical device.
days.projectBadge: 📝 Assessment: 15 MCQs (ES6+, async JS, React hooks, React Native core components, Flexbox).

curriculum.weekTitle: ⚡ Week 2 – Navigation, State Management & Native APIs

days.learning: 🎯 1h: Install @react-navigation/native and stack/tab navigators. Create a multi‑screen app with navigation between Home, Details, and Profile screens.
🎯 1h: Create a simple Theme or User context using React Context API. Consume context in multiple components to manage shared state without prop drilling.
🎯 1h: Install expo-image-picker. Implement a button that opens the device camera or gallery and displays the selected image on screen.
🎯 1h: Store and retrieve simple key‑value data (e.g., user preferences or a list of saved items) using AsyncStorage. Persist data across app restarts.
🎯 1h: Build a simple login/signup form with TextInput, validation (email, password), and form submission. Manage form state with useState.
🎯 1h: Overview of generating a signed APK for Android using Expo EAS Build. Understand the process for iOS (requires Apple Developer account).

days.dayName: Final Project: Note‑Taking or Task Manager App
days.learning: ✅ Build a complete app with the following features: ➤ User can add, edit, delete, and view notes/tasks. ➤ Use React Navigation with at least two screens (list screen + add/edit screen). ➤ Persist data locally using AsyncStorage (or SQLite if you want a challenge). ➤ Add at least one device feature (camera to add photo to note, or image picker for avatar). ➤ Implement a simple theme toggle (light/dark) using Context API. ➤ Deliver: Full Expo project, a short video demo, and a README explaining how to run the app.
days.projectBadge: 📝 Final Assessment: 20 questions (navigation, Context API, device APIs, AsyncStorage, forms, build process).

courseId.title: 🧑‍ Entrepreneurship for Service‑Based Company
courseId.description: Launch and grow a service business: consulting, agency, freelancing, or professional services. Covers client acquisition, pricing, delivery, operations, and scaling – essential for founders and independent professionals.

sessions.sessionName: Service Offering & Pricing: Define your first service package
Tuesday: Financial Management for Service Business
Final Project: 90‑Day Launch Plan: Operational roadmap for your service business

days.learning: 🎯 1h: Types: agency, consulting, freelancing, subscription services. Identify your skills → define a niche. Case studies: design agency, digital marketing freelancer.
🎯 1h: Craft a unique value proposition. Positioning statement (for whom, what problem, why you). Create a simple brand message.
🎯 1h: Pros/cons of each model. Value‑based pricing. Calculate your target rate (desired salary + overhead). Example pricing calculator.
🎯 1h: Outbound (cold email, LinkedIn, networking) vs inbound (content, SEO, referrals). Build a lead list. Outreach script template.
🎯 1h: Discovery call structure. Listen for pain points. Present solution. Write a winning proposal: scope, timeline, pricing, terms.
🎯 1h: Sole proprietorship vs LLC. Service agreement essentials (scope, payment terms, IP, liability). Non‑disclosure agreements (NDA).

✅ Create a complete service offering for a niche of your choice: ➤ Define target client persona. ➤ Write a value proposition and positioning statement. ➤ Design two pricing options (e.g., project fee and retainer). ➤ Draft a simple 1‑page service agreement (scope, payment, timeline). ➤ Deliver: PDF document (1‑2 pages) with service package + pricing + contract template.
days.projectBadge: 📝 Assessment: 15 MCQs (service models, pricing, lead gen, legal basics, proposals).

days.learning: 🎯 1h: Standardise your process (SOPs). Client onboarding workflow. Project management tools (Asana, Trello). Communication cadence.
🎯 1h: Track income/expenses. Profit margin. Cash flow management. Invoicing & payment terms (net 15/30). Simple P&L for a service firm.
🎯 1h: Onboarding experience, regular check‑ins, delivering value beyond scope. Requesting testimonials and referrals. Loyalty discounts.
🎯 1h: When to hire first employee or contractor. Roles: delivery vs sales vs admin. Systems for delegation. Freelancer platforms (Upwork, Fiverr).
🎯 1h: Content marketing (LinkedIn posts, blog, newsletter). Case studies & portfolio. Speaking at events. Building authority in your niche.
🎯 1h: Setting boundaries. Time tracking. Batching work. Pricing for profit to reduce hours. Systems for automation (Calendly, invoicing software).

days.topic: Operational roadmap for your service business
days.learning: ✅ Build a complete launch and growth plan: ➤ Niche, service package, pricing (from Week 1 project). ➤ Client acquisition strategy (channels, outreach plan). ➤ Delivery workflow (SOP for first project). ➤ Financial projections (first 3 months: expected revenue, costs, profit). ➤ One growth tactic (referral system or content plan). ➤ Deliver: 2‑3 page PDF + optional spreadsheet for financials.
days.projectBadge: 📝 Final Assessment: 20 questions (delivery systems, cash flow, hiring, retention, marketing, scaling).
